Quick summary (high level):
- Soft-Guarantee Pilot (recommended for first 8 weeks): 40 min GPUs, up to 2x burst, month-to-month billing for the pilot period. Soft guarantee = we reserve baseline capacity and provide preferential routing; credits for sustained unavailability (pro-rated SLA).
- Limited Commitment (6–12 month): 80 min GPUs with scheduled ramp to 160 over 90 days; includes warmup credits and 48-hour burst window.
- Firm Floor + Burst (12 month): 120 min GPUs baseline, 200 burst ceiling; lower unit price, 30% billed as committed capacity.

Key asks:
1) Confirm whether VelixSys treats US-west vs US-east as separate floors or a pooled floor (that affects minimum per-region GPU).
2) Are 2–4 weeks of canary traffic acceptable before increasing to the next tranche?
3) Any hard restrictions on preemption or strict on-prem latency SLOs we should bake into the routing policy?

If you want, we can turn the Soft-Guarantee Pilot into a short-term commitment with a fixed warmup credit line to simplify procurement. I left line items and a DocuSign link in the PDF.

Thanks — I can hop on a 30-min call this week to walk through trade-offs.

4) Warmup credits: can you add a one-time warmup credit line to the pilot to cover JIT model weight pulls and tokenization caching?

Also: Finance asked whether Redwood can supply a short justification memo for the 12-month Firm Floor option so we can present to our CFO. Procurement has procurement@velixsys.com on this thread — loop them in when you send the revised PDF.

Quick technical check: regional splits and routing are straightforward with two caveats:

1) Minimum per-region floors: we can implement a soft per-region floor (25/15 split for pilot) using affinity-based routing and a regional fallback. That means we reserve baseline instances in each AZ/region and prefer routing there; overflow will route to the other region if local floor is saturated.
2) Burst behavior: bursts are handled by autoscaling pools; if they exceed the soft floor, requests hit pay-as-you-go lanes. We can cap bursts with a blended-cap (billing smoothing) but that requires committing ~8–12% more committed capacity in the blended price to offset variability.
3) Canary/Rollback: 14-day canary is fine. For rollback we need a runbook (automated switch of routing policy + model variant fallback) — ops can effect rollback in under 24 hours if the issue is routing or model performance. If there’s a platform outage tied to infra, our SLA credit applies and we’ll coordinate with them.

Implications:
- Pilot 25W/15E soft floor is operationally cheap and preserves most of their west latency profile.
- If VelixSys requires a strict hard floor (no cross-region overflow), cost goes up ~18% because we must reserve cold capacity in both regions.

I’ll attach a short ops note for the canary runbook.

— Karthik
VP, Serving Runtime
